title: Gold, Futures Pricing & Market Trends - Systematic Investor 335 [REUPLOAD]

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Gold, Futures Pricing & Market Trends - Systematic Investor 335 [REUPLOAD].docx

speakers: Rob Carver (systematic futures trader and author)
summary: Rob Carver answers listener questions on leverage, markets vs systems, ETFs vs futures, signal scaling and missing data, then covers the Quantica sizing paper (volatility sizing, skew vs Sharpe) and a minutes-to-decades momentum/mean-reversion paper. Also discusses gold futures borrowing costs and macro consequences of Trump policies (higher inflation, higher risk premium).

coverage.note: gold futures carry and London to US gold flow
gold borrowing cost spike, mixed signals, multi-strat fees
pass-through fee drag, transparency, pod performance fees
early 2025 trend following performance by sector, trend barometer
index returns Feb 2025, leveraged ETF drag
leveraged ETF decay, Kelly, return stacking
markets vs systems, correlation, carry, capital
signals, ETF vs futures testing, costs, liquidity
total return comparison, ETF access, forecast scaling
regression and scaling, objective, CTA research
research frontiers: execution, alt data, ML, risk management
execution budget, discretionary trade lesson, mean reversion question
absolute mean reversion, Occam, EMA vs breakout
lag, weighting functions, overfit nonlinear
missing data and interpolation
Quantica position sizing paper, skew
Sharpe vs skew, geometric return
terminal wealth simulation, leverage caution
Safari and Schmidhuber time scale paper
momentum and mean reversion horizons, data
Trump macro: midterms, tariffs, deportation, supply chains
Trump macro: regulation risk premium, funding shocks, net view
lead-lag of bonds and gold vs equities, trust
policy lag, bond safety, fourth turning
nothing actionable: sign-off

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the Futures price will depend on the Spot Price Plus any kind of yield that you earn on it um you know less any interest rates funding the position
claims.claim: Gold has no yield, so its futures premium over spot is driven mainly by the borrowing (funding) cost, with storage cost small when spread over large inventories.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: according according to market reports what's happening is that um gold is basically um being moved from London to the US
claims.claim: Gold moving from London to US vaults (or ownership rights moving) created an inventory imbalance across warehouses in early 2025.
claims.testable: partly - based on market reports, unclear who is moving it

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they normally follow pretty closely the the sort of quote unquote risk-free rates you'd expect them to be about kind of four and a half 5%
claims.claim: Gold borrowing costs normally track the risk-free dollar rate of about 4.5-5%.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: but actually they they've jumped up S like 10 11 12% which is just you know crazy because of this this weird imbalance in inventories across warehouses
claims.claim: Gold borrowing costs jumped to 10-12% annualized (December future about 150 points over spot) because of warehouse inventory imbalance.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: so it's one of those weird situations where you're kind of getting mixed signals from the the price movement and the carry movement
claims.claim: He holds long gold, silver and bitcoin from trend, but carry is negative because futures trade well above spot, giving conflicting trend and carry signals.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they estimate clients effectively paying something like 7 and 20 or even up to 15 and 20
claims.claim: Bloomberg estimates multi-manager pass-through fund clients effectively pay 7 and 20 up to 15 and 20 once pass-through expenses are counted, versus a 2 and 20 benchmark.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: what the client got was 2.8%
claims.claim: A multi-strategy pass-through fund earned about 15.2% before fees in 2023 but the client received only 2.8% (caption ambiguous), illustrating large fee drag.
claims.indicator: net vs gross hedge fund returns

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there's all this money kind of Disappearing out the back door kind of almost invisibly
claims.claim: Multi-strategy pod funds charge expenses to client accounts outside headline fees, so institutions comparing headline fees underestimate costs; transparency has gone backwards compared with retail UCITS.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you'd have to pay performance fees to the managers that were doing well
claims.claim: In fund-of-funds and pod models, winning managers are paid performance fees even when the overall portfolio loses, ratcheting up costs.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the only thing I can kind of see from my vantage point that's been a little bit tricky this year has been the currency sector um and that's mostly been in February actually
claims.claim: In early 2025 the currency sector was the one tricky area for trend followers, mostly in February.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you would think things like eques have done well for Trend followers coffee even some of the metals you mentioned gold for sure
claims.claim: Equities, coffee, gold and some metals contributed for trend followers in early 2025 while CTA indices stayed near zero.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer finished yesterday at 30 which is actually a week reading
claims.claim: His Trend barometer reading of 30 signals weak trend strength in the market, a different measure from index returns.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: btop 50 is up uh 46 basis points as of Tuesday uh up 1.68% uh so far this year so that's actually doing uh the best of all of the indices
claims.claim: By mid-Feb 2025 trend indices were roughly flat (BTOP50 +1.68%, SG CTA +0.77%, SG Trend +0.57%), the short-term traders index was negative, MSCI World +3.79% and S&P 500 TR +3%.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, short-term traders index

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if they go down 10% and they go up 10% you actually end up down so you're not you know back where you started
claims.claim: Leveraged ETFs are dangerous for long holding because volatility drag makes down-then-up moves end below the start, worse with leverage.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: over a long period of time with very volatile assets is the the value of these will tend drift down
claims.claim: A leveraged ETF on a very volatile underlying such as Strategy (a levered bitcoin proxy) would be dragged toward zero over time.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the appropriate level of Leverage and risk depends on something called the the Kelly criteria
claims.claim: Appropriate leverage depends on the Kelly criterion, which uses expected performance of the asset or strategy.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the risk you're getting on something is more than about 20 25 30% it's potentially quite likely that that's going to be more than the amount of risk you should actually be taking
claims.claim: Rule of thumb: risk above about 20-30% volatility is probably more than justified by expected performance, so 2x S&P ETFs (30-40% vol) are too much while 1.5x 60/40 (about 12-15% vol) is fine.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if the correlation of of manag Futures and S&P stays relatively low then is going to have a lowish risk and then applying some leverage to it is going to be fairly safe
claims.claim: Return-stacked products (2x S&P plus managed futures) are safe only while the correlation between managed futures and equities stays low; if it rises, volatility exceeds a safe level.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it's quite likely you'll get more diversification from adding more markets than by adding further Trend falling systems
claims.claim: Adding markets gives more diversification than adding similar trend systems because of correlation.
claims.indicator: correlation of added market vs added trend system

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the extra Market is going and are probably going to have a correlation of 04.5 with the ones that are in there something like that another Trend following system would might have a correlation of 8.9
claims.claim: A new market has correlation about 0.4-0.5 to existing ones, whereas another trend system has about 0.8-0.9.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: at that point the the pendulum swings from you know more markets being better to a different system being better
claims.claim: Once a portfolio has many markets, a different style (e.g. carry, correlation about 0.5) adds more than further markets.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: adding systems is to be free as far as capital goes whereas adding markets isn't
claims.claim: Adding systems needs no extra capital if automated, adding markets does, though complexity rises.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I wouldn't just add a thousand different signals to my model just just because they all might produce a tiny marginal increase
claims.claim: Adding many signals with tiny marginal gains is not worth the complexity.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you're going to trade Futures then you really probably should be using Futures to actually testing with
claims.claim: Back test with the instrument you will trade: futures for futures, ETFs for ETFs (test what you trade, trade what you test).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: all the things being equal I would expect the ETF to cost more money
claims.claim: An ETF wrapper usually costs more than futures: fees, provider profit and higher slippage from size.
claims.indicator: ETF expense ratio vs roll costs

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of ETFs have been issued but they don't all have very good liquidity frankly
claims.claim: ETF liquidity is variable, which matters when substituting ETFs for futures.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: essentially you want to be Computing a what I'd call A A true Total return Series
claims.claim: Compare ETF and futures on total return: ETF includes dividends/interest less costs; futures back-adjusted prices need the risk-free rate added because margin earns interest.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the reason why you would want to go down the ETF route would potentially be Market access and contract size
claims.claim: ETFs are useful for market access and small contract size (fractional shares) when capital is limited, but with enough capital futures are better.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if it's positive then I'm bullish if it's negative I'm bearish
claims.claim: A signal (feature) is turned into a forecast by scaling it, like a z-score, so it says how big the forecast is.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the coefficient on the regression is going to be something that tells you how big the wiggly line is you know is this a big forecast or a small forecast
claims.claim: Regress volatility-normalized returns on the signal: the coefficient equals the forecast scaling, so regression and scaling are the same thing.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: that's just a way of essentially removing any systematic bias from forecasts that are systematically long or systematically short which you may not want to do by the way
claims.claim: The regression intercept removes systematic long or short bias, which he prefers not to remove.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I would always be trying to forecast risk adjusted returns
claims.claim: The target of a forecast should be risk-adjusted returns because positions are sized by risk.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: ctas that that you know have not changed their model for years not done any any research and just plugging in one quite quite happily
claims.claim: Some CTAs run unchanged models for years and it can still be a valid approach.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they could be doing things like for example implementing new markets
claims.claim: Research at big CTAs is often adding new markets (such as AHL Evolution), which can give the biggest return for effort.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the bigger bigger you are the more important execution is
claims.claim: Execution matters more as assets grow; a big fund trading billions notional should invest in execution.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: people looking at alternative sources of data and and that's also quite a big growth area
claims.claim: Alternative data is a growth area for research.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: but I'll be very wary of any any any sort of team of researchers that were purely you know focusing exclusive on that area of improvement
claims.claim: Neural networks and ML on existing data are less likely to add value; he is wary of teams focused exclusively on them (Renaissance excepted).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I don't think necessarily that uh as an industry we're coming up with many new ways of doing Trend following
claims.claim: Few new ways of doing trend following exist, but combining more than one approach (e.g. moving average crossover plus another) may give better results.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: where where I would suspect we see the most Evolution still and where there's still room to improve is probably risk management
claims.claim: Risk management and risk forecasting offer the most room for evolution in trend following.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's rare um that you hear about a trend follower blowing up uh unless it's specifically because they were running like a 5x leverage version of their strategy
claims.claim: Trend followers rarely blow up unless they run highly leveraged versions.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: probably of the research budget 35 40% of that goes to of course execution
claims.claim: AHL says 35-40% of research budget goes to execution to avoid losing out as inflows grow, raising strategy capacity.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I made made a good entry decision but a poor exit decision
claims.claim: His discretionary bond trade caught the yield top but was closed flat because he had no predefined stop or exit criteria; he concludes he should stay systematic.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the authors show that returns returns years 2 through five are negatively related to subsequent returns
claims.claim: Moskowitz et al. (2012) show returns in years 2 through 5 are negatively related to subsequent returns, supporting a long-term mean reversion signal.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the strategy has a negative sharp ratio but improves the performance of his Baseline Trend plus carrier strategy
claims.claim: Rob's five-year relative mean reversion strategy has a negative Sharpe but improves a baseline trend-plus-carry portfolio.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: which is just negative momentum um so this should definitely work
claims.claim: Absolute long-term mean reversion (negative multi-year momentum) should work in principle and is simpler than relative mean reversion and probably diversifying.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there's a long-term signal it's going to be quite hard to get statistical significance
claims.claim: Long-term signals are hard to show significant and may show a negative Sharpe in a back test.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in terms of aom's Razor you know should always go for the simplest possible version of something
claims.claim: Prefer the simplest version of a strategy (Occam's razor).

claims.speaker: Listener Samuel (question read by Niels)
claims.quote: systematically don't change back tests all that much on a diversified basket
claims.claim: EMA crossovers versus Donchian breakouts give similar back tests on a diversified basket.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: we can reduce it by using less of the past and more recent periods
claims.claim: All indicators lag; lag can be reduced by shorter windows or weighting recent periods more, as in an EMA.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: both the moving average and exponential moving average and indeed any indicator that takes series of past returns is is a waiting function over those past returns
claims.claim: Moving averages and EMAs are weighting functions of past returns (flat or exponential).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'm not generally a fan of um sort of nonlinear stuff um because it it's it it's not very intuitive and also it's highly potentially highly it could be highly overfit
claims.claim: Nonlinear responses to recent observations add parameters and risk overfitting.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I've judged that the complexity they add is not worth the tiny tiny insignificant performance that they had
claims.claim: A separate short-horizon mean-reversion signal added tiny insignificant performance and was not worth the complexity.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the easiest thing to do is to ignore any data before February 2023 so basically ignore the period it was trading earlier and you know obviously ignore the Gap
claims.claim: When contracts are delisted and relisted, the simplest approach is to ignore data before relisting.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you'd be trading this thing until due 2020 and then you'd go to a position of zero until the price prices started coming in again
claims.claim: Better is a trading system that handles missing data by going flat until enough prices exist to form forecasts and volatility.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I would really really not interpolate data price data and then use that in a back test and say oh yes look at this is great I think it's a fundamentally stupid thing to do
claims.claim: Do not interpolate missing prices in back tests; 99.9% of the time it is wrong.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: estimating um a volatility and you've got hourly data but obviously you've got a period when markets are closed then it's probably a reasonable thing to do to get a better estimate of volatility
claims.claim: Interpolating is reasonable only for volatility estimation across overnight hours, using a Brownian bridge rather than cointegration/ECM.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the third methodology is the methodology I use which is to say I want I want to get a certain number amount of risk on my contract
claims.claim: Three position-sizing methods: fixed contracts, fixed notional, and fixed risk (volatility-scaled); Quantica finds volatility adjustment has the highest Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they come to the conclusion that the volatility adjustment has the highest shot ratio
claims.claim: Volatility-adjusted sizing has the highest Sharpe ratio (cocoa 2024 example).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the closer to your sort of fixed position sizing the system you're running or even the noal position sizing the the greater the the ski you'll get
claims.claim: Fixed-contract or fixed-notional sizing produces more positive skew (explosive moves like cocoa hit an unscaled position), as losers are closed.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: effectively the price of risk is is basically zero for a leverage Trader we can get any amount of risk that we want to get
claims.claim: For leveraged futures traders volatility can be scaled freely so Sharpe is the measure, but skew cannot be created by leverage.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: be something like um a equity Market neutral strategy they they tend to have um negative skew as well
claims.claim: Option selling and equity market neutral strategies have high Sharpe but negative skew, unlike trend following.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the amount of Shar ratio you should be giving up to sort of quote unquote buy positive skew was actually very small
claims.claim: The Sharpe ratio worth sacrificing to buy positive skew is small, so the higher Sharpe strategy is generally better.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: maximizing that basically maximizes the am amount of money that you have at the end of at the end of your investment Horizon
claims.claim: The geometric mean return (CAGR) maximizes terminal wealth and should be the key metric.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: Shar ratio you know only works if everything has the same skew
claims.claim: Sharpe ratio is valid only when compared strategies have the same skew.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: conceivable amount of improvement in skew that would justify that that lower shot ratio
claims.claim: The lower Sharpe from constant-contract or constant-notional sizing cannot be justified by skew improvement.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the additional benefits of of having a higher shot ratio massively more than compensate for the fact that we're not getting those big upside volatility moments
claims.claim: Simulating terminal wealth for different Sharpe and skew combinations shows the benefit of higher Sharpe outweighs lost upside volatility, so Sharpe can be optimised despite penalising upside volatility.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: we should always be careful of high shot ratio strategies that require a lot of Leverage
claims.claim: Be cautious of high-Sharpe strategies that need much leverage or are opaque, since the back test may hide negative skew risk (Madoff).

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: momentum seems to work well um empirically um certainly in Futures across multiple asset classes for time periods of say a month up to a year
claims.claim: Momentum works empirically across futures from about a month to a year, while multi-year periods show mean reversion.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: mean reversion tends to work well because that's where the high frequency Traders are operating
claims.claim: At very short horizons mean reversion works because HF traders buy bid and sell ask around a bouncing price.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: for time periods of less than an hour mean reversion occurs okay um and the most I think the most me verion occurs at um roughly a five or five minute time window
claims.claim: Safari and Schmidhuber find mean reversion at horizons below an hour, strongest around 5 minutes.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: trading at those kinds of frequencies is a massive engineering and back testing exercise and it's not something that you should be casually doing
claims.claim: Trading at 5-minute mean reversion horizons needs large engineering and testing effort.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they look at probably the widest range of of time frequencies I've seen in any paper ever
claims.claim: The paper fits a cubic polynomial across a very wide range of time frequencies to classify each horizon as momentum or mean reversion.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: as long as long as you're not really a really fast Trader you should probably be a momentum Trader
claims.claim: Momentum prevails from about one hour out to one year (days, weeks, months), supporting CTAs.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: anything longer than a year is is when mean reversion kicks in
claims.claim: Beyond a year the data show mean reversion, so a 2-4 year horizon favors a mean reversion strategy.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they look at data out 16 years and they're still finding mean reversion out there and to do that they're looking at data from 1692
claims.claim: The paper uses data from 1692, about 330 years, and finds mean reversion out to long horizons.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: trading costs in particular are going to be very hard to overcome if you Trend following it short time frequencies
claims.claim: Trend following at short frequencies is hard because trading costs are hard to overcome.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: two years is pretty much flat so you might get away with 18 months
claims.claim: Trend lookbacks up to about 18 months may work; one year is strong and two years flat in the paper.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: majorities in the midterms that happens nearly all the time mainly because people just don't like sitting you know they don't like sitting governments
claims.claim: A president who starts with majorities usually loses one in the midterms, so Trump has about two years to legislate.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: they won't just increase inflation the US will increase inflation globally I think um for sure you know would due to retaliation
claims.claim: Tariffs increase inflation in the US and globally through retaliation.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: simple supply and demand if you reduce the amount of Labor uh in the market um then that will probably increase wage costs
claims.claim: Mass deportations cut labor supply and lift wages, adding to inflation.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: what covid really showed us is that the the sort of network of Supply chains in the world is a very delicate and delicate thing
claims.claim: Supply chains are fragile, so deportations and tariffs may cause shortages and inflation.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: Us cars bits of cars go backwards and forwards between Canada and and the us across the border
claims.claim: Tariffs on integrated US-Canada auto supply chains would be inflationary.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: increase um you know what in Economist will call the risk premium so people will demand to be paid more um to hold risky assets
claims.claim: Unstable regulation, rule of law and frequently changed tariffs increase the risk premium, which is bad for equities.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: potentially it's going to make people unemployed it's going to cause Supply shocks it's going to cause demand shocks it's going to cause uncertainty
claims.claim: Stopping government payments could cause unemployment, supply and demand shocks and uncertainty.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it's going to be bad for equities I think there going to be inflation which is going to be Bann for bonds
claims.claim: Net view: policy uncertainty hurts equities and inflation hurts bonds, which favors CTAs.
claims.direction: short equities and bonds; long CTAs

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we see the risk show showing up in only parts of the financial uh markets at the moment right uh so fixed income is probably showing uh a little bit more concern about what's going on
claims.claim: Fixed income and gold price in risk from Trump policies while equities show little angst.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: an erosion of trust erosion of trust in institutions
claims.claim: Erosion of trust in institutions over decades makes a disconnect between value and price.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a price-based strategy that doesn't care about is it the right value or not but just follows the price
claims.claim: Where price and value disconnect, a price-following strategy like trend following is a good portfolio component.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the equity markets for a long time thought everything was fine yeah um and it was in the the the bond markets and the debt in the you know the CDs markets
claims.claim: In 2007-08 credit, mortgage and bond markets signalled trouble before equities.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the bond market could be a bit ahead of the curve and maybe even the gold market
claims.claim: Bond investors are more professional and conservative than equity investors (more retail now), so bonds and gold may lead equities on Trump risks.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there'd be quite a lag before they have an effect on the real economy and uh and start showing up in things like you know jobs numbers and and even bigger lack before they show up in equities
claims.claim: Trump policy effects reach jobs data with a lag and equities even later, so watch and wait.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I would not be surprised if what people think is safe I.E government bonds will turn out to be not so safe
claims.claim: Government bonds may prove unsafe and equities a safe harbor in a public-private cycle turn (not a market forecast).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the books uh that he or the book he wrote uh back in the early 90s the fourth turning I think that is a concept that we should not ignore at this
claims.claim: The Fourth Turning generational cycle suggests the period will turn more turbulent before it ends.
